items.title: Autonomous cooling of Kerr-cat qubits to minutes-long bit-flip times
items.abstract: Quantum error correction becomes more hardware efficient when physical noise is strongly biased towards one error channel. Cat qubits realize such a bias by encoding information in two opposite coherent states of a superconducting oscillator, so that bit flips are exponentially suppressed with photon number while phase-flip rates increase only linearly. In Kerr-cat qubits, a driven double-well potential confines these states and enables fast coherent control, but excitations can induce interwell switching, limiting bit-flip times to milliseconds. Here we show that the nonlinear interaction generating the confinement can also cool these excitations. When an intra-well transition becomes resonant with a lossy readout mode, excitations are transferred out of the qubit and dissipated, as established by spectroscopy and relaxation measurements. We observe the predicted exponential scaling of Kerr-cat bit-flip times with photon number, reaching 450 s, over five orders of magnitude beyond previous demonstrations. Phase-flip rates remain consistent with intrinsic photon loss at operating points with seconds-long bit-flip times. We further demonstrate fast Z gates without measurable degradation of bit-flip protection and single-shot readout with a bit-flip probability below $10^{-6}$ per measurement. Autonomous cooling thus brings minutes-long bit-flip protection to Kerr-cat qubits while retaining fast coherent control, without additional cooling drives or circuit elements.
items.why: Resonant cooling through a lossy readout mode extends Kerr-cat bit-flip times to 450 s, five orders beyond earlier demonstrations.

eli5.plain: They made the bit-flip errors of a cat qubit so rare that one takes minutes on average.
eli5.how: Heat-like excitations inside the qubit's double-well normally cause switching; tuning an intra-well transition onto a lossy readout mode drains them, so bit flips are suppressed exponentially with photon number as theory predicts.
eli5.matters: Strongly biased noise is what makes cat-qubit error correction cheap, and this removes the millisecond ceiling that had limited Kerr cats.
eli5.caveat: Phase flips still grow with photon number, and the gate set and codes built on such qubits remain to be shown.

items.title: Observation of Inter-Transition Interference
items.abstract: Many well-known quantum interference phenomena are associated with coherent superpositions of quantum states. Recent theoretical work showed that dissipative coupling between transition coherences can give rise to a distinct form of quantum interference in open quantum systems, termed inter-transition interference (ITI). Here we experimentally observe ITI through coherent microwave reflection spectroscopy of a superconducting artificial atom realized by a Kerr parametric oscillator. Using strong parametric driving, we access a regime in which two transitions become nearly degenerate and simultaneously contribute to the reflected response. The observed spectral lineshapes are not adequately captured by a model of independent transitions. By contrast, theoretical calculations that incorporate dissipative coupling between the corresponding transition coherences reproduce the essential features of the measured spectra. These results provide experimental evidence for ITI and demonstrate that dissipative coupling between transition coherences can qualitatively modify spectroscopic responses. More broadly, our work identifies transition coherences as a new arena for quantum interference in open quantum systems.
items.why: Reflection spectra of a Kerr parametric oscillator near a degeneracy need dissipative coupling between transition coherences; independent-line models fail.

eli5.plain: They shone microwaves on a driven superconducting artificial atom and saw spectral lines that only make sense if two transitions interfere through their shared loss.
eli5.how: Strong parametric driving pushes two transitions of a Kerr parametric oscillator almost on top of each other; the reflected microwave lineshape is then fit with and without a term that couples the two decaying coherences, and only the coupled model works.
eli5.matters: It is a new interference channel in open-system spectroscopy of artificial atoms, so lineshapes you might blame on extra modes or noise could instead be this effect.
eli5.caveat: The evidence is a better model fit to reflection spectra at one operating point, not an independent signature such as photon statistics.

items.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
items.abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.
items.why: Log-depth interferometric time-bin mixing reshapes any known single-photon waveform into one common mode with >99.9% overlap.

eli5.plain: They design an optical device that reshapes single photons of different shapes into a common shape so they can interfere.
eli5.how: The photon is split into time bins; programmable couplers and delays interfere bins pairwise, concentrating the amplitude into one short bin in log₂N stages.
eli5.matters: Waveform matching between unlike emitters is the same problem as catching shaped microwave photons between nodes; the time-bin approach is a template.
eli5.caveat: Simulation only, and loss per stage dominates at large N.

items.title: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
items.abstract: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive. Dissipation and environmental noise have prevented such control in the inherently low-frequency domain of free-particle dynamics---a regime of growing importance for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Here we realize a suspended 1-milligram rotor operating in the free-particle regime with exceptional environmental isolation. Combining this isolation with a low-noise measurement architecture, we directly resolve thermal fluctuations in the motion associated with a damping rate of only 7~nHz. Through continuous quantum measurement of the rotor, we localize its otherwise unconfined motion, obtaining conditional states with entropic temperatures as low as 140~nK as a quantitative measure of control in the free-particle regime. This is two orders of magnitude below temperatures previously achieved in tabletop optomechanical experiments. We demonstrate immediate utilities of the new operating regime, setting new constraints on modifications of quantum mechanics and benchmarking inferred entanglement-to-decoherence rate ratios nearly two orders of magnitude beyond the state of the art for tests of gravity at the quantum-classical interface.
items.why: Continuous measurement of a 1 mg free rotor with 7 nHz damping reaches conditional states at 140 nK entropic temperature.

eli5.plain: They held a milligram object nearly free of friction and used measurement alone to pin down its motion very precisely.
eli5.how: A suspended torsion-free rotor is isolated so well that its thermal motion is visible; a low-noise optical readout continuously tracks it, and the conditional state is narrow.
eli5.matters: Quantum control of free masses is the route to gravity and collapse tests; the measurement-based control mirrors feedback in circuit QED.
eli5.caveat: Conditional states are not ground-state cooling, and 140 nK is still far from the quantum regime for this mass.

items.title: The Reference System Loophole
items.abstract: I argue that the Extended Wigner's Friend theorems have a `loophole' that has previously not been appreciated, coming from the fact that we typically need a reference system to give meaning to a measurement outcome. I show how this loophole can be used in the context of the Local Friendliness theorem to preserve the predictions of quantum mechanics without denying Local Friendliness, and I respond to some objections. I explain how the loophole arises naturally from consideration of relevant symmetry transformations, and then I appeal to the partial/complete observables formalism to argue that the same loophole will work for any type of Wigner's Friend experiment, even if it is performed with a variable that does not obviously look like it requires relativization to a reference system. Finally I compare the loophole to other possible responses to the Local Friendliness theorem, and I show that the same loophole will work for other Extended Wigner's Friend theorems too.
items.why: Outcomes need a reference system to mean anything; relativising to it keeps quantum predictions and Local Friendliness both.

eli5.plain: She argues that Wigner's-friend no-go theorems quietly assume outcomes are absolute, when they only make sense relative to a reference object.
eli5.how: Using symmetry transformations and the partial/complete-observables formalism, she shows outcome records can be relativised so the theorem's premises do not jointly hold.
eli5.matters: Extended Wigner's friend tests are being planned with small quantum agents; this says what such a test could and could not rule out.
eli5.caveat: Philosophical argument; whether the loophole is natural or ad hoc is debatable.

items.title: Quantum-Nondemolition Probing of Multiphoton Transitions between Dressed States in a Strongly Driven Jaynes--Cummings System
items.abstract: The response of the Jaynes--Cummings (JC) model to strong driving has been examined previously, but the origin of intriguing features near emitter--cavity resonance remains poorly understood because of the large background in conventional transmission spectroscopy. Here we introduce a spectroscopic approach for circuit quantum electrodynamics that combines strong cavity driving with quantum-nondemolition qubit readout. Separating the drive and readout substantially enhances the measurement sensitivity as compared with conventional cavity-transmission spectroscopy. With this technique, we identify the near-resonant features as multiphoton transitions between emitter--photon dressed states of the same parity, and resolve transitions between dressed states of opposite parity. Away from resonance, we also observe selective enhancement and suppression of multiphoton transitions, together with transitions involving the second excited state of the anharmonic qubit. Our approach opens a route to resolving the rich transition structure of the JC ladder and probing strongly driven light--matter interactions.
items.why: Separating strong cavity drive from QND qubit readout resolves same- and opposite-parity multiphoton dressed-state transitions up the Jaynes-Cummings ladder.

eli5.plain: They mapped the many-photon transitions of a strongly driven qubit-cavity system much more cleanly than transmission measurements allow.
eli5.how: The cavity is driven hard to climb the ladder of qubit-photon dressed states, then the qubit is read out separately and non-destructively, which removes the large transmitted background that hides weak features.
eli5.matters: It is a practical spectroscopy trick for circuit QED that exposes structure near resonance which had been ambiguous, including transitions through the transmon's second excited state.
eli5.caveat: It identifies transitions rather than measuring the emitted light, and the assignments rely on modelling of a single device.

items.title: Recoverability of Gravitational Entanglement under Decoherence
items.abstract: Decoherence can make gravitationally generated entanglement arbitrarily small, or even vanishing, without necessarily rendering the effective matter dynamics separable. We ask whether this hidden non-separability can be revealed using strictly local quantum error correction. For Newtonian gravity supplemented by physically relevant localization noise, including environmental noise, and noise from collapse models such as GRW, CSL, and Diósi--Penrose, we analyze when the underlying entangling resource is locally recoverable. For GRW- and CSL-type noise, we analytically establish that strictly local quantum error correction can make the ratio of the effective gravitational interaction strength to the residual decoherence rate arbitrarily large for any parametrization of the collapse model, even in regimes where the unencoded entanglement signal approaches zero. By contrast, the Diósi--Penrose model does not exhibit the same enhancement under bipartite protocol considered here, revealing a qualitative difference. These results show that the loss of detectable entanglement is not equivalent to the loss of a recoverable non-separable resource, and open a route toward practical recovery protocols.
items.why: Local error correction can recover gravitational entanglement hidden by GRW/CSL noise, but not under Diósi-Penrose.

eli5.plain: They show that even when collapse noise hides gravity-made entanglement, local error correction can bring it back, except for one collapse model.
eli5.how: The noise may leave the underlying dynamics non-separable; encoding each mass locally suppresses the effective decoherence relative to the gravity coupling for GRW and CSL.
eli5.matters: It gives a way to tell collapse models apart in gravity-entanglement experiments.
eli5.caveat: Assumes ideal local codes on massive systems, far from current capability.

items.title: Analog quantum simulation of paraparticle statistics
items.abstract: Bosonic and fermionic quantum statistics describe all known elementary and emergent particles in three dimensions, although many attempts have been made to discover other valid quantum statistical frameworks. One recent formulation proposes "$R$-paraparticles," indistinguishable particles with nonlocal internal degrees of freedom governed by generalized exchange rules [Wang and Hazzard, Nature 637, 314 (2025)]. Here, we emulate a species of paraparticle that exhibits a generalized Pauli exclusion principle using a superconducting qubit lattice. We confirm its unique quantum statistics by measuring a $180^\circ$ phase shift under paraparticle exchange, observing antibunching independent of internal degrees of freedom under two-particle interference at a beamsplitter, and finding a thermal occupation inconsistent with both Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics. These results demonstrate that parastatistics are observable on quantum simulation platforms, further motivating their use to explore theorized new phases of matter.
items.why: A qubit lattice emulating R-paraparticles shows a 180° exchange phase, antibunching and non-Bose non-Fermi thermal occupation.

eli5.plain: They used a grid of superconducting qubits to imitate particles that are neither bosons nor fermions and checked that they behave that way.
eli5.how: Excitations in the lattice are dressed with internal degrees of freedom so their exchange rule matches a recent paraparticle proposal; exchange phase, beamsplitter interference and thermal statistics are measured.
eli5.matters: It shows analogue simulators on superconducting chips can test exotic statistics, with Hong-Ou-Mandel-style interference as the probe.
eli5.caveat: These are emulated paraparticles in an engineered lattice, not new elementary particles.

items.title: All-to-All Connectivity in Superconducting Qubits via Metamaterial-Mediated Interactions
items.abstract: We show that encoding superconducting qubits as dual-rail or spin-locked transmons lets a metamaterial waveguide couple them all-to-all while suppressing the spurious entanglement that burdens shared-mode architectures, a step toward the non-local connectivity that quantum low-density parity-check codes require. In a bare-transmon architecture, the dispersive coupling between each populated mode and every idle qubit attached to it entangles spectators with the gate, and cancelling it by dynamical decoupling lengthens every gate. The encoding suppresses this coupling at the hardware level, from second to fourth order in the inverse qubit--mode detuning. A two-tone cross-resonance drive then generates a Mølmer-Sørensen interaction between encoded qubits, which we use for an entangling gate and a joint parity measurement, both selective and parallelizable through different modes. Simulating two dual-rail transmons sharing three resonators with a mode lifetime of $30\,μ$s, we find that heralding transmon relaxation as erasure leaves a gate infidelity of $1.4\times10^{-3}$ at $152$~ns, dominated by photon loss. Photon loss and mode crowding together bound the array size. The gate duration must exceed the inverse mode spacing, which shrinks as the array lengthens, while photon loss grows with gate duration. This bound grows linearly with the mode lifetime and with the inter-resonator coupling; at a lifetime of $150\,μ$s, five times the simulated value, and a coupling of $80$~MHz, a $10^{-3}$ error budget admits $13$ qubits on $25$ resonators.
items.why: Dual-rail or spin-locked transmons on a metamaterial waveguide get all-to-all gates with spectator coupling pushed to fourth order.

eli5.plain: They propose wiring many superconducting qubits to each other through a shared waveguide without the qubits disturbing one another.
eli5.how: Encoding each qubit in two modes cancels the dispersive shift of idle qubits to leading order; a two-tone drive then gives an entangling interaction through chosen waveguide modes.
eli5.matters: Non-local connectivity is what quantum LDPC codes need, and this gives a hardware route from a group with metamaterial experiments.
eli5.caveat: Simulations of two qubits and three modes; scaling and mode crowding are untested.

items.title: Dynamically modulated light-matter interactions for ancilla-tolerant bosonic control
items.abstract: Strong light-matter interactions are central to state-of-the-art quantum technologies, spanning platforms as diverse as Rydberg atoms, trapped ions, and superconducting circuits. In superconducting circuits, the strong dispersive coupling between microwave photons (light) and ancillary qubits (matter) has enabled universal bosonic control and quantum error correction. However, this always-on dispersive interaction propagates errors from the ancillary qubits to the bosonic systems both while idling and when performing operations, introducing a trade-off between control strength and fidelity. We break this trade-off by introducing a parametrically activated hybridization between the bosonic modes and ancilla qubits, keeping both elements decoupled when not active. When activated, this hybridization mediates a dynamic light-matter coupling with non-trivial engineered symmetries, permitting resilience to ancilla decay and dephasing. This dynamic coupling functions as a new control primitive that offers a route to bosonic processors whose performance is set by the oscillator, rather than the ancilla.
items.why: Parametrically activated hybridisation couples bosonic modes to ancillas only when needed, with symmetries making control tolerant to ancilla decay.

eli5.plain: They propose a way to control microwave-cavity qubits so the helper qubit's errors do not leak into the cavity.
eli5.how: Instead of an always-on dispersive coupling, a parametric drive turns on a hybridisation with built-in symmetry, so ancilla decay or dephasing does not corrupt the oscillator.
eli5.matters: It could let bosonic processors be limited by cavity quality rather than by transmon ancillas, a recurring bottleneck.
eli5.caveat: Theory and design; the experimental gain is not yet shown.

items.title: Quantum-enabled measurement of gravitational forces at the milligram scale
items.abstract: Gravity is by far the weakest among all known interactions. While it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe, gravitational interactions between small masses in the microscopic range remain underexplored because they are too weak to be experimentally accessible. The interface between gravity, described by general relativity, and quantum mechanics, which describes the microscopic world, is of particular interest. From a theory standpoint, these two major descriptions of nature have not been combined in a satisfactory manner. Technology is gradually becoming mature enough such that probing gravity at the microscopic scale, where quantum mechanics and gravity potentially meet, is becoming accessible. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. Here, we present an experiment at millikelvin temperatures, where the gravity due to a micron-range coherent displacement of an 87 mg source mass imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass. Vibrations of the membrane are measured in the microwave optomechanical scheme, which is a key setup for investigating non-classical motional states of mechanical oscillators. When considering the combination of total source and test masses, our setup presents two orders of magnitude progress in sensing gravity at the small scale, as well as a 35 dB improvement of gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above. Our setup offers a plausible approach for studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states.
items.why: Millikelvin optomechanics detects gravity from a micron-scale moving source mass at the milligram scale.

eli5.plain: They measured the gravitational pull between small masses inside a dilution refrigerator.
eli5.how: A source mass is moved coherently by microns, and a cold mechanical sensor read out with quantum-limited techniques picks up the gravitational force.
eli5.matters: Getting gravity measurements into the same cryostats as quantum circuits is a step toward gravitationally coupled quantum systems.
eli5.caveat: The masses are classical here; quantum gravity tests need non-classical states.

items.title: The Structure of Shared Classical Facts in Quantum Systems
items.abstract: Perfectly matching local outcomes need not constitute a nondisturbing shared classical record. For finite-dimensional multipartite states, we prove that nontrivial exact records are equivalent to a spectrum sharing structure with a unique finest decomposition into locally distinguishable sectors, where entanglement may persist. For a fixed complete pointer, exact sharing is equivalent to strong quantum Darwinism together with global nondisturbance, while spectrum broadcast structure additionally requires conditional independence. Arbitrarily weak full-rank admixtures eliminate exact sharing, but two-sided distance bounds quantify robustness through disturbance and disagreement, while information bounds connect accurate local readouts to observer consensus.
items.why: Exact shared classical records are equivalent to spectrum-sharing structure; arbitrarily weak noise destroys exact sharing.

eli5.plain: He proves when several observers can truly share the same classical fact about a quantum system.
eli5.how: Exact nondisturbing records require a unique decomposition into locally distinguishable sectors; this equals strong quantum Darwinism plus nondisturbance, with bounds for the approximate case.
eli5.matters: It sharpens the quantum-Darwinism story of how objective facts emerge.
eli5.caveat: Finite-dimensional theorems; robustness is only via bounds.

items.title: Boson sampling is fragile to loss
items.abstract: Boson sampling experiments aim to demonstrate quantum computational advantage with increasing numbers of interfering photons. A central question is whether their computational hardness survives under photon loss. We show that even an arbitrarily small nonzero uniform loss rate permits efficient classical sampling in the average case when the rate remains fixed as the system grows. We exploit how loss suppresses correlations involving many photons to approximate the full output distribution using low correlation orders. The resulting samplers run in time polynomial in system size and inverse total variation error, with the error averaged over Haar random interferometers. The results apply to Fock state boson sampling with single-photon states in distinct input modes and arbitrary additional vacuum inputs, and to Gaussian boson sampling with equal squeezing of bounded strength in every input mode. Classical sampling is efficient even when the mean detected photon number grows linearly with system size, showing that large photon counts alone do not ensure computational hardness.
items.why: Any fixed nonzero uniform loss lets boson sampling be classically simulated efficiently on average.

eli5.plain: They show that losing even a small fraction of photons makes boson-sampling experiments easy for an ordinary computer.
eli5.how: Loss suppresses many-photon correlations, so the output distribution is well approximated using only low-order correlations, which is cheap.
eli5.matters: It sharpens what photonic or microwave sampling experiments must achieve to claim advantage.
eli5.caveat: Average-case result for fixed loss rates; loss that falls with system size is not covered.

items.title: Ground-State Dressing and Delayed Feedback of a Chiral Giant Atom in Ultrastrong Waveguide QED
items.abstract: We study a chiral giant atom ultrastrongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide at two spatially separated points. At a relative coupling phase π/2, the total spectral density is independent of the distance between the coupling points, whereas its directional components are not. Using a variational polaron transformation, we show that the renormalized transition frequency and the total ground-state dressing inherit this independence, while the virtual-photon cloud remains chiral. A sudden switch-off of the coupling releases this cloud as directional radiation. We also derive the spontaneous-emission dynamics in the polaron frame, showing that, after neglecting the local photonic potential, the memory kernel becomes distance independent at the same phase.
items.why: At coupling phase π/2 a chiral giant atom's dressing is distance-independent but its virtual-photon cloud is directional and can be released.

eli5.plain: For an atom touching a waveguide at two points, they find a setting where its energy shift ignores the distance but its bound photons still prefer one direction.
eli5.how: A polaron treatment of ultrastrong coupling shows the total spectral density cancels distance dependence at phase π/2, while each direction's component does not.
eli5.matters: Giant atoms and ultrastrong coupling are natural in superconducting circuits, so this predicts a directional burst on switching off.
eli5.caveat: Theory with approximations; switch-off speed needed is demanding.

items.title: Breakdown of Linearized Dispersion in Waveguide QED
items.abstract: Exploring interactions between quantum emitters and guided photons, waveguide quantum electrodynamics (wQED) offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation and quantum interconnect. To simplify the quantized light-matter interactions, a linearized dispersion approximation (LDA) was widely used in wQED under the conditions of weak coupling and narrow photonic bandwidth. However, a growing number of strong-coupling wQED experiments have called the validity of LDA into question. Here, by investigating giant atoms coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide, we propose a principle to judge the validity of LDA. We find that the decoherence of the atoms exhibits rich dynamical behaviors determined by different numbers of bound states in and out of the continuum (BICs and BOCs) formed in the energy spectrum of the total atom-photon system. Based on this, we show that despite the LDA can partially preserve some of BICs, it completely erases BOCs. This causes the dominant role of LDA in the atomic dynamics to break down. Providing a physical insight into the validity of LDA, our results lay a firm foundation for exploring fundamental physics and its application frontier in strong-coupling wQED platforms.
items.why: Linearised dispersion erases bound states outside the continuum for giant atoms, so it fails at strong coupling.

eli5.plain: They show a standard simplification of waveguide physics throws away important bound states when coupling is strong.
eli5.how: Using the full waveguide dispersion, giant atoms form bound states inside and outside the band; linearising keeps some inside but none outside.
eli5.matters: Circuit waveguide QED routinely reaches the strong-coupling regime where this matters for modelling.
eli5.caveat: Specific semi-infinite giant-atom geometry.

items.title: Resetting a Superconducting Qubit with a Compact Colder Resistive Dissipator below the Qubit Frequency
items.abstract: Efficient qubit reset has become a key requirement for large-scale superconducting quantum processors, as initialization fidelity increasingly lags behind gate performance and quantum error correction demands rapid, high-fidelity state re-initialization. This work proposes a compact on-chip dissipator consisting of two transmon dissipation modes and a thin-film resistor, and experimentally demonstrates an unconditional reset protocol. With no additional control lines and negligible impact on the qubit $T_1$, the effective temperature of the transmon qubit is reduced from $49$~mK to $35$~mK. Quantum process tomography is employed to benchmark the reset process, achieving a process error of $0.0028$. This reset protocol is robust to pulse parameter deviations, thereby relaxing calibration requirements. The dissipator architecture provides a practical, calibration-friendly reset solution for large-scale superconducting quantum processors.
items.why: An on-chip thin-film resistor below the qubit frequency cools a transmon from 49 to 35 mK with 0.0028 reset process error.

eli5.plain: They added a small cold resistor on chip that resets a qubit without extra control lines.
eli5.how: Two auxiliary transmon modes route qubit energy into a thin-film resistor that is colder and lower in frequency than the qubit, giving unconditional reset.
eli5.matters: Fast, simple reset is increasingly the weak link in error-correction cycles.
eli5.caveat: One device; reset speed and its scaling to many qubits are not the headline.

items.title: Collectively pumped superradiant laser with coherence scaling beyond the standard quantum limit
items.abstract: For more than half a century, the standard quantum limit (SQL) was thought to limit the laser coherence $\mathfrak{C}$ -- the number of photons emitted from the laser into the beam in one coherence time -- to a scaling $Θ(μ^2)$, where $μ$ is the mean number of optical-frequency excitations stored inside the laser. However, recently it has been shown [Baker et al., Nat. Phys. 17, 179 (2021)] that the Heisenberg limit -- an achievable ultimate limit set by quantum mechanics for the task of producing a beam with the standard properties of a laser beam -- is $\mathfrak{C}=Θ(μ^4)$, a quadratic enhancement. So far, proposals to demonstrate beyond-SQL scaling of $\mathfrak{C}$ have been limited to circuit QED, at microwave frequencies (i.e., a maser). Here, we introduce a class of generalized far-above-threshold (FAT) laser models, obtained by replacing the ordinary bosonic lowering operator $\hat{a}$ by a general lowering operator $\hat{L}$ in the superoperators appearing in the master equation that governs the FAT laser dynamics. We then show that an optical-frequency superradiant laser in the bad-cavity limit, with feedback-controlled collective pumping, realizes one such model, in which $\hat{L}$ is identified with the collective superradiant lowering operator $\hat{J}$. This model can surpass the SQL scaling, with the coherence exhibiting a scaling as large as $\mathfrak{C}= Θ(μ^{8/3})$ in the optimal parameter regime. Here, in the bad-cavity limit, $μ\approx N/2$, where $N$ is the number of superradiant atoms.
items.why: Generalised far-above-threshold laser models show an optical superradiant laser can reach Heisenberg-limited coherence scaling, previously proposed only for masers.

eli5.plain: They show that a laser built from many atoms emitting together could produce a beam far more coherent than the textbook limit allows.
eli5.how: They replace the photon lowering operator in a standard laser master equation with a collective atomic one and show the beam coherence then scales as the fourth power of stored excitations, not the square.
eli5.matters: The earlier beyond-limit proposals were circuit-QED masers; this widens the idea and gives microwave experimenters a cleaner theoretical frame for the same target.
eli5.caveat: It is model-level theory; the required collective pumping is idealised and no experiment is close.

items.title: Geometric Pumping of Optical Work in Coherent Wave Scattering
items.abstract: Optical work exchanged between light and time-varying matter underlies a wide range of emerging photonic technologies, yet a general geometric theory describing its generation and control has been lacking. Here we establish such a theory for coherent electromagnetic scattering. We show that the net optical work accumulated during an adiabatic modulation cycle is a geometric quantity determined by the Berry curvature of the outgoing field in parameter space. Nonzero optical work can thus be generated by cyclically modulating two or more independent system parameters. In contrast to conventional adiabatic pumping between incoherent reservoirs, optical work pumping vanishes under maximally mixed illumination. Greater illumination coherence increases the maximum work attainable through wavefront shaping. For fully coherent illumination, we derive the optimal incident wavefront and modulation trajectory that maximize the optical work per cycle. Our framework unifies time-varying photonics, optomechanics, and geometric transport within a common scattering formalism.
items.why: Cycled scattering parameters pump optical work equal to Berry curvature of the outgoing field; vanishes for incoherent light.

eli5.plain: They show that slowly cycling a scatterer's properties extracts energy from light in an amount set by geometry.
eli5.how: The work per cycle is an integral of a Berry curvature in parameter space; with coherent light and the right wavefront it is maximised.
eli5.matters: Time-modulated microwave circuits are an ideal testbed for such geometric pumping.
eli5.caveat: Classical-wave theory; no experiment.

items.title: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED
items.abstract: We investigate the emission profiles of singly excited collective states and propose a matched-mode witnessing protocol in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single-photon wavepacket, providing a route to state verification through the common waveguide output. We identify the emission mode associated with a chosen target state and employ an auxiliary virtual-cavity representation to evaluate the quantum state of this selected output mode. For a matched initial state, the selected mode contains the emitted single photon, whose Wigner function exhibits a pronounced non-classical negative dip, serving as a distinct fingerprint of the target many-body state. With the reference mode held fixed, different initial configurations yield different photon occupations and phase-space distributions, demonstrating the state selectivity of the protocol. These results connect collective-state verification with temporal-mode analysis of the emitted radiation, offering access to collective coherence with reduced reliance on qubit-resolved correlation measurements.
items.why: A mirror-terminated waveguide's output photon mode carries a collective excitation's phases; a negative Wigner dip witnesses the target state.

eli5.plain: They propose checking which collective state a group of emitters is in by looking at the shape of the photon it emits.
eli5.how: Amplitudes and phases of the collective excitation imprint on the emitted wavepacket; filtering the matched temporal mode gives a single photon with negative Wigner function only for the target.
eli5.matters: Matched-mode capture and Wigner tomography of itinerant photons are standard in circuit QED, so this is directly testable there.
eli5.caveat: Ideal-loss theory with a virtual-cavity tool.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.abstract: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.
items.why: Autler-Townes dressing reshapes anharmonicity for a 97 ns all-microwave CZ gate at 99.40% fidelity.

eli5.plain: They use a strong drive to shift energy levels and make a fast two-qubit gate with fixed-frequency qubits.
eli5.how: Dressing a non-computational level via the Autler-Townes effect changes the qubit's nonlinearity without touching the computational states, enabling a fast low-leakage CZ.
eli5.matters: All-microwave gates avoid flux noise, and this is another lever for fixed-frequency architectures.
eli5.caveat: 99.4% is below current CZ records; errors are mostly decoherence.

items.title: Single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain: beyond independent radiation
items.abstract: We study single-photon scattering by a nanofiber-coupled atomic chain, comparing a full microscopic model with an independent-radiation approximation. We show that nearly equal transmission probabilities can coexist with substantially different transmitted temporal modes, even after adjusting their relative delay. For a reference chain, a decomposition into collective atomic resonances relates this discrepancy mainly to spectral-phase changes caused by the omitted interatomic couplings. Parameter scans delimit this phase-dominated regime, and controlled comparisons separate the effects of coherent exchange and collective decay.
items.why: Nanofiber atomic chains can give equal transmission but different transmitted temporal modes once interatomic coupling is included.

eli5.plain: Two models of light passing an atom chain agree on how much gets through but disagree on the pulse shape.
eli5.how: Comparing full microscopic and independent-radiation models shows interatomic couplings mainly change spectral phase.
eli5.matters: Temporal mode matters for anything that later interferes the photon, as in networks.
eli5.caveat: Theory comparison on one setup.

items.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
items.abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2π$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole contributions in atoms exhibiting only electric dipole transitions. This eliminates the need to simultaneously excite pure electric-dipole and magnetic-dipole responses with exactly matched radiation. We derive a two-mode model for this response and show that it accurately captures full coupled-dipole simulations near the optimal lattice spacings. Because of the wide applicability of coupled-dipole models, the relevance of our microscopic analysis extends beyond atomic physics to nanostructured metasurfaces. Moreover, the same platform also connects directly to established subradiance-protected single-photon storage protocols, suggesting a route toward combining wavefront engineering, storage, and retrieval in a simple atomic bilayer.
items.why: A two-atom-unit-cell bilayer lattice acts as a near-ideal Huygens surface with full 2π phase control.

eli5.plain: They show a simple atom-array arrangement that transmits all light while letting you set its phase.
eli5.how: Collective modes of the bilayer supply both even and odd radiation channels, mimicking electric and magnetic dipoles.
eli5.matters: Metasurface concepts with collective emitters could inspire arrays of superconducting atoms on waveguides.
eli5.caveat: Proposal requires precise atomic arrays.

items.title: Flux Crosstalk Calibration from Zero Knowledge to High Precision in Fully Tunable Superconducting Circuits
items.abstract: Precise and independent flux control is essential for scalable superconducting processors built from frequency-tunable qubits and couplers, but flux crosstalk undermines it. Conventional calibration methods rely either on dedicated readout channels, which tunable couplers typically lack, or on readout schemes requiring extensive prior spectroscopy of the qubit and coupler. We demonstrate two independent methods that characterize coupler flux crosstalk without directly driving or measuring the couplers. The first method is zero-knowledge characterization, which exploits intrinsic coupler-resonator coupling to yield rapid and accurate estimates with no prior qubit or coupler spectroscopy, accelerating large scale bring-up. The second method is symmetric branch cancellation, which isolates crosstalk from other dispersive effects allowing for quantifying with high precision. Combined with an improved iterative procedure, these methods suppress residual coupler crosstalk below $5\times10^{-5}$, providing a complete route from zero-knowledge initialization to high-precision crosstalk characterization in fully tunable architectures.
items.why: Two methods calibrate coupler flux crosstalk without reading couplers, reaching residuals below 5e-5.

eli5.plain: They found ways to measure unwanted flux leakage onto couplers that have no readout of their own.
eli5.how: One method uses the coupler's weak coupling to resonators for a quick estimate; the other cancels symmetric spectral branches for precision.
eli5.matters: Crosstalk calibration is a major bring-up cost for tunable-coupler processors.
eli5.caveat: Calibration tooling; benefit is in speed and precision, not new physics.

items.title: Gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave source limited by thermal noise
items.abstract: Josephson junctions are compact on-chip sources of coherent microwave and terahertz radiation, but conventional radiators couple the emission frequency, output power and dissipation through a single bias voltage. Here we demonstrate a gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave radiator based on a graphene weak link integrated with a separately gated graphene shunt resistor. The bias voltage sets the Josephson frequency, while the local gates tune the Josephson current and the total device resistance, enabling electrostatic control of emitted power at a chosen frequency. The device resolves Josephson harmonics up to fourth order, and its radiation power scales with source current and impedance as expected from a lumped-element circuit model. We further show that the emission linewidth is quantitatively described by Johnson-Nyquist noise at the electron temperature. The linewidth therefore provides an on-chip thermometer under bias, with the resistance-dependent heating captured by a minimal heat-balance model based on Wiedemann-Franz diffusion and electron-phonon coupling.
items.why: A graphene Josephson radiator decouples emission frequency from output power with gates, and its linewidth is set by Johnson noise.

eli5.plain: They built a tiny on-chip microwave source whose frequency and power can be tuned separately with electric gates.
eli5.how: A graphene Josephson junction emits at a frequency set by the bias voltage, while gated graphene resistors tune the junction current and impedance, and hence the power.
eli5.matters: A compact tunable on-chip source and a built-in electron thermometer (via the linewidth) are useful parts for cryogenic microwave setups.
eli5.caveat: The output is classical, thermally broadened radiation, not quantum light, and the linewidth is far from what a qubit drive needs.

items.title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
items.abstract: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.
items.why: Modelling shows electro-optic transduction plus optical photon counting could raise axion-haloscope scan rates 5-10x over quantum-limited homodyne.

eli5.plain: They work out how well a haloscope could count dark-matter-made microwave photons by converting them to optical photons first.
eli5.how: A microwave-to-optical transducer moves the cavity signal to light where single-photon counters are good; overcoupling the microwave cavity trades efficiency for lower transducer noise.
eli5.matters: It is a concrete use case and noise budget for transducers as microwave photon counters, which competes with qubit-based counters.
eli5.caveat: Projected gains use parameters from different devices combined into one hypothetical device.

items.title: Efficient preparation of spin-squeezed states with Grover's algorithm
items.abstract: We propose a scheme for preparing spin-squeezed states in an ensemble of $N$ spin-$1/2$ particles based on Grover's algorithm. With only a few oracles, the scheme can exactly prepare superpositions of a few neighboring Dicke states with the Wineland squeezing parameter scaling as $N^{-1}$. The scheme requires only global rotations and Dicke-selective phase shifts, thus avoiding the need to engineer a dedicated many-body Hamiltonian for the squeezing dynamics. We further discuss the feasibility of realizing the scheme in cavity QED systems, with the phase-matched Grover iterations realized by single-photon reflection from a dispersively coupled cavity. Full-sequence scattering calculations accounting for finite photon bandwidth and loss show that appreciable spin squeezing can be achieved with high fidelity for suitable system parameters.
items.why: A few Grover iterations with Dicke-selective phases prepare spin-squeezed states with N^-1 scaling.

items.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
items.abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear $(χ^{(2)})$ source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as $N^{3/2}$, where $N$ is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of $N^2$. At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as $N^2$. In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.
items.why: Quantised, depleting pump changes optimal sensing: Heisenberg scaling appears at maximal depletion, not maximal squeezing.

items.title: Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a delocalized massive shell
items.abstract: We construct a model for the response of a detector to vacuum fluctuations inside a massive hollow shell in a superposition of positions. The delocalized source mass gives rise to a superposition of spacetime geometries and their associated vacuum fluctuations. To describe this system, we employ the formalism of quantum reference frames to transition to a frame in which the source mass occupies a definite position while the detector is in a superposition of positions. This allows the dynamics of the detector to be analyzed using standard tools of quantum field theory on a definite curved spacetime. We compute the detector response for a wide range of configurations of the shell and detector positions and investigate how information about the quantum state of the shell is encoded in the response function, identifying features of the superposition that are effectively captured by the detector. In particular, we show that, under appropriate postselection, the response function exhibits interference patterns, and identify regions of the parameter space of the model in which the shell-induced contributions to the interference terms are maximized.
items.why: A detector inside a mass shell in superposition shows postselected interference in its response, via quantum reference frames.

eli5.plain: They calculate what a tiny detector sees inside a hollow mass that is in two places at once.
eli5.how: Switching to the mass's frame puts the detector in superposition on a definite spacetime, so standard field theory applies.
eli5.matters: It is a model for how gravity-source superpositions could imprint on quantum probes.
eli5.caveat: Idealised; effects need postselection.

items.title: Time- and phase-resolved emulation of sign-selective counterdiabatic dynamics in a superconducting qutrit
items.abstract: In cyclic three-level systems, phase-sensitive interference can convert a coupling-sign reversal into a population contrast, providing a controllable analogue of handedness. We emulate this mechanism in a superconducting transmon qutrit using two resonant single-photon drives and a phase-controlled effective two-photon drive. Effective loop phases \(Φ_L=+π/2\) and \(Φ_R=-π/2\), separated by \(π\), reverse the auxiliary contribution to the dark--bright coupling, canceling the intrinsic nonadiabatic term for \(L\) and reinforcing it for \(R\). Time-resolved trajectories reveal dark-pathway transfer for \(L\) and bright-manifold participation for \(R\). Measured late-time averages give a target-state population contrast of 0.929. Loop-phase measurements establish phase selectivity, while pulse-area and common-mode amplitude scans characterize the operating regime and control sensitivity. These results provide direct time- and phase-domain access to sign-selective counterdiabatic interference in a programmable cyclic qutrit.
items.why: Loop phases of ±π/2 in a driven transmon qutrit switch counterdiabatic interference on or off, giving 0.93 population contrast.

eli5.plain: They used a three-level superconducting circuit to mimic how a 'handedness' sign can steer population transfer.
eli5.how: Two single-photon drives and an effective two-photon drive form a loop; the loop phase either cancels or reinforces the non-adiabatic coupling, sending population through a dark or a bright path.
eli5.matters: It is a clean demonstration of phase-controlled three-level interference, the same toolbox as STIRAP-style control of transmons.
eli5.caveat: It is an emulation of chiral discrimination, not a measurement on molecules, and the physics is known Λ/Δ-loop interference.

items.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
items.abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.
items.why: A kinetic-inductance TWPA gives over 30 dB gain at 300-700 MHz with 2.5-3.5 quanta system noise.

eli5.plain: They built a near-quantum-limited amplifier for frequencies below 1 GHz.
eli5.how: A long kinetic-inductance line is pumped so a weak signal gains energy from the pump as it travels.
eli5.matters: Sub-GHz readout matters for spin qubits, detectors and axion searches; it extends parametric amplifiers downward.
eli5.caveat: Noise is a few quanta, not at the limit, measured in one setup.

items.title: Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting electronics
items.abstract: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top $α$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rmα$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $μ$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rmα$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.
items.why: Alpha-Ta/TaOx SIS junctions made on 150 mm foundry tooling show 2% critical-current spread across a chip.

eli5.plain: They made tantalum Josephson junctions in an industrial process with good uniformity.
eli5.how: Seed layers make the low-loss alpha phase of tantalum grow for both electrodes, and room-temperature probing estimates critical currents.
eli5.matters: Tantalum improves qubit coherence; all-Ta junctions could remove aluminium loss.
eli5.caveat: No qubit coherence data yet.

items.title: Nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system
items.abstract: Directionally generating and controlling quantum states is critical in chiral quantum technologies. Here, we propose a scheme for the nonreciprocal generation of Bell states via cooperative dissipation in a qubit-magnon system, consisting of a superconducting transmon qubit and a yttrium iron garnet sphere subject to a bias magnetic field. The cooperative dissipation between them is induced by coupling both to a common transmission-line waveguide. Due to this cooperative dissipation, the system possesses a dark eigenstate within the single-excitation subspace. Under appropriate parameter conditions, the dark eigenstate reduces to a specific Bell state. With the assistance of a drive pulse, the system can be prepared in this Bell state (i.e., the dark eigenstate). In particular, we find that the dark eigenstate corresponds to different Bell states under positive ($+\mathbf{B}_0$) and negative ($-\mathbf{B}_0$) bias fields. Consequently, nonreciprocal Bell-state generation is achieved: $+\mathbf{B}_0$ yields one Bell state, while $-\mathbf{B}_0$ yields the other. Moreover, we define a fidelity-based nonreciprocal rate to quantify this nonreciprocity. Our work establishes cooperative dissipation as a versatile resource for nonreciprocal entangled-state generation, opening a promising route toward chiral quantum technologies.
items.why: A transmon and a YIG sphere sharing a waveguide have a dark state that becomes a different Bell state for each bias-field direction.

eli5.plain: They propose making a qubit and a magnet's spin wave entangled, with the field direction choosing which entangled state you get.
eli5.how: Both systems leak into the same transmission line, so their decay interferes and leaves one dark state; magnon chirality makes that dark state field-direction dependent.
eli5.matters: It is a waveguide-QED way to make nonreciprocal entanglement in hybrid circuits.
eli5.caveat: Proposal only; magnon damping and YIG integration with transmons are the hard parts.

items.title: Superradiance fingerprints of moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel
items.abstract: Hybrid moiré excitons form a dense array of electrically tunable single-photon emitters, entailing cooperative optical responses with intriguing consequences. With the strong dipole-dipole interaction, they also realize Bose-Hubbard quantum simulators of emergent correlated matter such as Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC). Here we reveal the characteristic cooperative radiation from condensates of hybrid moiré excitons in twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayers. In each individual moiré trap, the layer hybridization selection rule dictates that the ground-state exciton is a quantum emitter of orbital-angular-momentum photons, with an exceptionally long radiative lifetime. Ground-state emission becomes pronounced only upon forming condensates, where inter-sublattice dipole attraction and intra-sublattice repulsion together lead to the coexistence of exciton and biexciton BEC with comparable weights. The biexciton (molecular-type) BEC decays through superradiance of path-entangled biphotons, whereas the exciton (atomic-type) BEC is dark at rest and becomes superradiant when it carries a supercurrent. Our findings not only uncover a novel source of entangled light but also establish unique fingerprints for exploring the cold chemistry of atomic-molecular condensates with moiré excitons.
items.why: Moiré exciton-biexciton condensates radiate path-entangled biphotons or supercurrent-enabled single photons.

items.title: Coulomb Blockade in a One-Dimensional Array of Strong Josephson Junctions
items.abstract: We measure current across a voltage-biased, long array of Josephson junctions. Current-voltage characteristics do not reveal any critical current and instead display the presence of threshold voltage and finite activation energy, consistent with the Coulomb blockade. However, the respective energy scale is well below the value prescribed by a single-island geometric capacitances. We explain it by strong quantum fluctuations of charge associated with a large value of Josephson energy, $E_J\gg E_C$, where $E_C$ is the charging energy associated with the inter-island capacitance. Comparison between the data and theory points to an exponential (in parameter $E_J/E_C$) suppression of the threshold. We achieve a quantitative agreement with theory by accounting for charge-$e$ solitons associated with the quasiparticles entering the array from its leads. This scenario however underestimates the current below threshold in comparison with the experiment.
items.why: A long array of strong Josephson junctions shows Coulomb blockade with a threshold exponentially suppressed in EJ/EC.

eli5.plain: A chain of junctions that should superconduct instead blocks current below a small voltage.
eli5.how: Quantum charge fluctuations shrink the blockade energy exponentially; quasiparticle-related solitons entering from the leads explain the data.
eli5.matters: Long junction arrays are the superinductors in fluxonium and similar circuits, so their charge physics matters.
eli5.caveat: Theory underestimates the subthreshold current.

items.title: Exponential suppression of bit-flip errors in dissipative cat qubits
items.abstract: We study the infinite-dimensional Lindblad generator $L_ε=D[a^2-α^2]+εD[a]$, describing a dissipative cat qubit subject to single-photon loss. For sufficiently large $α$ and sufficiently small $ε>0$, we identify a two-dimensional spectral subspace near zero and establish an upper bound on the slow decay rate that decreases exponentially with $α^2$, uniformly in $ε$. This proves exponential suppression of bit-flip errors.
items.why: Rigorous spectral proof that dissipative cat qubits with photon loss have bit-flip rates exponentially small in α².

items.title: Persistent level-resolved transmon population after dispersive readout, and the limits of its open-system description
items.abstract: We calculate the level-resolved transmon population remaining after dispersive readout with a converged open-system model. The drive and qubit-cavity coupling use the rotating-wave approximation, while the cavity is a quantized mode in a frame displaced by its classical trajectory. At a readout occupation of 80, the model leaves a persistent distribution across the first transmon levels, with p2 = 1.02 x 10^-3 and p3 = 4.10 x 10^-5 at the end of readout. These populations survive an additional drive-off wait: over 73 ns each level decays by less than 3 percent and follows its own relaxation rate, not the near-factor-of-two drop in residual cavity photons. This identifies the population as bare-level occupation rather than coherent dressing. Channel-removal and bath-model controls attribute p2 mainly to dephasing and p3 and above mainly to relaxation, unchanged across bath models though absolute values vary by up to 15 percent. We also test the coherent drive truncation. In dissipation-free transmon-only benchmarks driven by the classical cavity trajectory, the nearest-neighbour RWA drive underestimates the full charge-operator result while the drive is on. At switch-off for occupation 80, where coherent populations are hundreds of times larger than the residual values, p2(RWA)/p2(full) = 0.905 and p3(RWA)/p3(full) = 0.759, with larger discrepancies at deeper levels. One source is a parity-allowed non-nearest-neighbour charge matrix element omitted by the drive operator. A naive beyond-RWA extension with bare-basis Lindblad dissipators fails a zero-drive ground-state test and serves only as a diagnostic. A dressed-basis (secular) construction instead leaves the dressed ground state stationary at zero drive. The result is a converged RWA prediction of readout-induced population plus direct tests of where the approximation loses quantitative reliability.
items.why: Converged open-system model finds p2≈1e-3 transmon leakage persisting after strong dispersive readout, from dephasing.

items.title: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors
items.abstract: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. We show that spatial-derivative coupling eliminates both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities of any spatial dimension, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively and even with initial correlations with the zero mode. Time derivatives and moving-detector rest-frame spatial derivatives can retain zero-mode state dependence not compromising causality. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.
items.why: Coupling detectors through spatial field derivatives removes zero-mode ambiguity in cavity particle-detector models while keeping causality.

eli5.plain: They show a way to model a detector in a cavity that does not depend on an unphysical, ambiguous cavity mode.
eli5.how: A detector coupled to the spatial derivative of the field never touches the zero-frequency mode, so predictions do not depend on its assumed state.
eli5.matters: In superconducting circuits, current coupling is this kind of coupling, so relativistic-QI proposals on circuits get cleaner.
eli5.caveat: Mainly a modelling clarification for free scalar fields in idealised cavities.

items.title: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals
items.abstract: Quantum memory is a core enabling device for large-scale quantum networks, serving as the fundamental building block for quantum repeaters and transportable quantum memories. Among various physical platforms, rare-earth-ion-doped crystals stand out as one of the most promising solid-state candidates for long-lived photonic quantum memories, owing to their exceptionally long spin coherence time and their compatibility with integration. In this review, we first introduce the physical mechanisms underlying long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth systems, with particular emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling techniques. We then review the experimental progress in this field, highlighting three distinct lifetimes--the spin coherence time, the light storage time, and the quantum storage time--and covering experiments that have achieved hour-scale spin coherence, minute- to hour-scale light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges that hinder the realization of practical long-lived quantum memories, explore potential strategies to overcome these obstacles, and outline the prospects for their future applications in quantum networks.
items.why: Review of rare-earth-doped crystal memories with hour-scale spin coherence and minute-scale quantum storage.

items.title: Inducing cooperative dynamics in an inhomogeneous many-emitter ensemble with a pulse sequence
items.abstract: Driving a many-particle quantum system with an appropriately tuned external field can give rise to features in its nonequilibrium dynamics that are absent in the equilibrium counterpart. Cooperative dynamics in a dense ensemble of quantum emitters manifested through superradiance, a burst in the emission intensity as a function of time, is typically suppressed by spectral disparities among emitters in the ensemble. We demonstrate the enhancement of cooperative dynamics in a spectrally inhomogeneous ensemble of quantum emitters when it is driven by a periodic pulse sequence. Using both a semi-analytical mean-field solution and a digital quantum simulation, we examine the coherence of the pulse-driven ensemble and the intensity of the emitted radiation as a function of the spectral disparity in the ensemble, as a function of time, the number of atoms in the system, and as a function of the inter-pulse delay. We identify clear signatures of the enhanced cooperative dynamics for the pulse-driven inhomogeneous ensemble when dephasing in the dynamics of the ensemble is suppressed by a sufficient number of pulses during the individual emitter lifetime. These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.
items.why: Periodic pulse sequences restore superradiance in spectrally inhomogeneous emitter ensembles.

items.title: Performance analysis of cat and GKP breeding protocols with squeezed single-photon input
items.abstract: Homodyne breeding is a promising optical route for generating large cat states and Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) grid states, using readily available squeezed-cat states as inputs. We analyze the performance of protocols, using squeezed single-photon seeds, $\hat{S}(r)\ket{1}$, as squeezed-cat resources and propagating them through the same cat-to-GKP breeding pipeline. For a symmetric tree with $N=2^{m_1}$ seeds, the heralded resource state reduces to a state with a polynomial-Gaussian wavefunction controlled by a single effective width, achieving near-unit fidelity with the desired cat resource state. Our analysis yields closed-form even-cat fidelities and an inverse-design rule for the seed squeezing. We apply these resources to GKP breeding, and find a large overlap with a practical GKP state. We also investigate the effects of practical imperfections, including finite homodyne acceptance windows and photon loss. This study shows that squeezed single-photon inputs provide a viable resource assignment for homodyne cat and GKP breeding, replacing the demanding requirement for high-resolution photon-number-resolving heralding with an on-demand single-photon source.
items.why: Squeezed single photons as seeds for cat and GKP breeding give near-unit fidelity cat resources.

items.title: Discovering Models for Experimental Quantum Systems with Agentic AI
items.abstract: A central obstacle in realizing color center cavity-QED-based quantum technologies is inhomogeneity, or disorder, among individual emitters. As the number of emitters increases, so does the complexity of the experimental data, making it difficult to quantify the present physical mechanisms of disorder. Here we introduce an artificial intelligence-driven model discovery framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent, equipped with tools and a structured workflow, proposes candidate Hamiltonian and Lindbladian models, generates computational tools, and quantitatively evaluates competing physical hypotheses. We apply the workflow to three previously published experimental cavity-QED datasets collected from color centers in diamond and silicon carbide. Across the experiments, the agent successfully identifies physical models for the system and characterizes the disorder. In assessing reproducibility, we find that run-to-run variability is concentrated primarily in the research plan generation step, while the computational analysis itself is substantially more consistent. Our results suggest that structured LLM agent workflows can support model discovery from quantum optical experimental data while simultaneously allowing for human expert supervision and collaboration.
items.why: LLM agent proposes and tests Hamiltonian models for disorder in color-center cavity-QED data.

items.title: Quantum Advantage needs Multiple Perspectives
items.abstract: The origin of the quantum speedup is a topic of ongoing research. We propose a logical criterion for the possibility of a speedup within the continuous-variable and odd-prime qudit settings. There, Wigner function nonnegativity signals the possibility of efficient classical simulation in the state-injection scenario. We consider representations of quadrature/Weyl measurements in a single von Neumann algebra that reproduce the Born statistics in a particular state. If in that state, the set-theoretic universe of the algebra is ZFC-satisfiable, i.e. every ZFC-theorem holds with unit probability, all measurement contexts can be represented in a single commutative algebra of `beables'. Furthermore, the statistics admit a noncontextual hidden variable model, ensuring Wigner nonnegativity for two or more modes or qudits. For a single mode, a stronger notion of linear representation ensures commutativity, and with it, ZFC-satisfiability independently of the state, as well as Wigner nonnegativity. In consequence, in any setting that cannot be efficiently simulated, it must be impossible to merge the models associated with every context into a single ZFC-satisfiable one: quantum advantage needs multiple perspectives.
items.why: Links quantum speedup to the failure of a single commutative beable algebra satisfying ZFC.

eli5.plain: He argues computational speedup appears only when no single classical description of all measurements works.
eli5.how: If one von Neumann algebra represents all quadrature measurements with ZFC holding, there is a noncontextual model and a nonnegative Wigner function.
eli5.matters: Links contextuality, a foundations notion, to where speedup can come from.
eli5.caveat: Formal-logic framing; restricted to CV and odd-prime qudits.

items.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
items.abstract: Cooper pairing is a fundamental aspect of superconductivity and results in charge transport with a basic unit of 2e (e is the electron charge). This basic unit can manifest itself as the denominator in the formula for Shapiro steps of ac Josephson effect-nhf/(2e), where h is the Planck constant, f is the ac frequency and n is an integer. Violation of this standard formula may suggest unconventional physics, such as nhf/4e for charge-4e superconductivity. Here, we report discovery of a new sequence of nhf/3e in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions. The microwave frequency/power, temperature, and current annealing dependences of this exotic sequence consistently point to hf/3e as the unit for Shapiro steps, indicating a Josephson tunneling process involving a trio of electrons (3e). This bunching of an odd number of charges distinguishes itself from well-established superconducting processes, which are carried by composite bosons made of an even number of charges. The unusual observations highlight the important interplay between competing charge orders in twisted bilayer systems.
items.why: Twisted cuprate Josephson junctions show Shapiro steps at hf/3e, pointing to three-electron tunneling.

items.title: Agentic Pipelines for Mapping Topological Codes to Quantum Hardware
items.abstract: Mapping a prescribed many-body Hamiltonian to a particular quantum hardware is generally an approximate process, resulting in both intended and unwanted quantum dynamics. We introduce an AI-agent-assisted workflow that uses Lean to establish whether an effective device Hamiltonian retains the intended low-energy subspace of the target many-body Hamiltonian. We demonstrate this approach with topological quantum error correction (QEC), providing, to our knowledge, the first Lean-verified pipeline connecting a code space to low-energy states of a device model. Starting from qubits and parity checks, the pipeline constructs the ideal Hamiltonian whose lowest energy states form the intended code space, and determines the excitation gap that protects that code space. It then tests if the device retains the required number of isolated low-energy states and quantifies how closely their subspace matches the intended code space. We compare three bounds on unwanted energy shifts obtained by: summing the interaction strengths, grouping the anticommuting Pauli interactions, and diagonalizing the Hamiltonian. Pauli grouping yields a bound that is tighter than the conventional sum and closer to the diagonalization result, avoiding overly conservative compensation requirements. The workflow also identifies the strongest unwanted interactions and the qubits they affect, providing specific targets for improving device couplings and controls. We demonstrate our framework using an eight-qubit toric-code array on a superconducting device, where the same driven device generates both the required four-qubit interactions as well as unwanted dynamics. An AI agent identifies viable device parameters within a prescribed leakage budget, and Lean verifies four isolated low-energy states close to the ideal code space. Our workflow supports predictive hardware engineering for analog implementations of QEC codes.
items.why: An AI-agent workflow with Lean verifies whether a device Hamiltonian keeps a topological code's low-energy space.

items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
